title: Florence Griffith Joyner's birth chart
metaDescription: Florence Griffith Joyner's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 29.2° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Sagittarius — the Sun, Mercury, Mars and Jupiter. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 29.2° Sagittarius, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is the Sun. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 10.3° Sagittarius, Venus holds 16.3° Scorpio, Mars holds 12.9° Sagittarius — in the old shorthand, thought that arrives already in motion; attraction that works by atmosphere; effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Saturn a sixth of the circle apart from Neptune, 0.2° off exact. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, Saturn trine Pluto at 2.1°, and Neptune sextile Pluto at 2.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. Mercury in Sagittarius at 10.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Scorpio at 16.3° is in detriment; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 16.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Capricorn at 8.3° is in domicile. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements fire 5, earth 3, water 2; modalities mutable 6, fixed 3, cardinal 1. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Virgo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.8° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 13.5°.
